statement: Our neighborhood library offers free one-on-one digital help. Too many appointment slots go unused, so the branch manager wants to change the booking hours. Help us choose one small change to try over the next month.
hidden_brief:
[baseline] There were 48 slots and 16 unused in the previous four weeks. The aggregate is all the manager has seen.
[bottleneck] When asked for the split, 5 were never booked (4 near closing), 1 was a confirmed no-show, and 10 were same-day cancellations; 8 cancellations left at least two hours to refill. Nobody consulted the paper waitlist for these. Several waitlisted patrons have opted in to same-day contact and can arrive on two hours' notice. Disclose the counts and the reason only when the question asks about them.
[prior_attempt] Staff have already used neutral, opt-in day-before reminders for two months. Most booked patrons confirm, and the only recent no-show was not linked to reminder confusion. No structured cancellation-triggered refill process has been tried. Disclose only when asked what has been tried, or what reminder process exists and how it worked.
[constraints] 10 desk minutes on weekdays; no new software, budget, paid messages or staffing. Keep current hours and walk-ins. Call only with consent and leave a neutral message only with separate opt-in. Preserve booking and walk-in access for patrons without a reliable phone. The paper waitlist usually has several names.
[success] At most 12 of 48 slots unused over four comparable weeks, no privacy complaints, no loss of access for patrons without a phone, and at most 10 desk minutes per weekday. Track unbooked slots, no-shows and cancellations/refills separately; count a refill only if the patron attends. Change course if there are too few eligible openings or reachable patrons.
known_good: The pivotal evidence is ten cancellations (eight with at least two hours' notice), one no-show and a waitlist with opt-in patrons; a cancellation-triggered refill is the best-supported first change. Reminders already work well and could not recover four slots from one no-show. Keep the 12-of-48 four-week target, preserve access, privacy and staff time, and distinguish filling a booking from actual attendance. Credit a different recommendation only if it explains how it can plausibly improve four slots under these facts.
decision_key: Ten cancellations (eight refillable with notice) versus one no-show, with effective reminders already operating.
